- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 3–5 days.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33), model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% for next 3–5 days.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 75% of recent 5-day high), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at +2% above recent peak for next 3 days.  
- If sentiment swings sharply from positive to negative, model often fails to adjust; apply mean reversion to forecast 3–5 days ahead, targeting 1–2% below recent 10-day average.  
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently overestimates in high-sentiment periods; apply 1–2% downward correction if sentiment > 0.67 for 3+ consecutive days.  
- If sentiment is neutral (0.00–0.33) and price is trending, model often misses mean reversion; adjust forecast to align with 10-day moving average.
